floor_history.headline: Sibling func_800483DC base-routing idiom drops floor 11->10 (clean pure C); c/d sign-extend fix killed (cascades to 22 via v1-walker scratch collision).
Floor held at 10; RTL-confirmed the residual is a combine lh-fold wall (c,d fold to lh; forcing lhu+sll+sra evicts the walker), and a 10.6k-iter permuter campaign found no zero.

frontier.hypothesis: A C structure that separates c,d's load from their sign-extension the way ABI arg-setup separates a,b's, so combine cannot fold c,d into lh, WITHOUT introducing a dead store or reversing evaluation order.
frontier.mechanism: a,b reach lhu+sll+sra because their zero-extended load and their (s16) cast are far apart in the insn stream (arg-reg setup interposes). If c,d's u16 values are forced to reside in a register across an intervening real computation before the stack store, combine may leave lhu+sll+sra while the walker stays in v1.
frontier.next_probe: Route c,d through a register-resident intermediate that is genuinely used (e.g. participate in the entry+=base or count computation ordering), or reorder so the c,d sexts are emitted after entry+=base with maximal load/sext distance; sandbox each and read the RTL to check both (a) no lh fold and (b) walker retained in v1.

frontier.hypothesis: The original source declared a,b,c,d as short struct fields and the target's uniform lhu+sll+sra comes from a specific field-access/type shape, not from per-value casts.
frontier.mechanism: Uniform treatment of all four halfwords in target suggests a homogeneous array/struct read; the fold difference is positional (stack vs reg), not type.
frontier.next_probe: Model the source as reading a[0..3] from a short/u16 array or struct and passing (s16) of each; sandbox and compare the c,d region against target.

frontier.hypothesis: This is an RA/scheduling tie that may be owner-gated if the separated-load structural axis is measured dead.
frontier.mechanism: If no pure-C spelling reconciles c,d-as-lhu+sll+sra with walker-in-v1, the remaining gap is a combine/RA tie akin to the endgame-lock cluster.
frontier.next_probe: Exhaust the separated-load and struct-array axes above; if both measured dead with the walker still evicted, consider owner-escalation per endgame-lock-disposition-policy (few-insns-short, combine-fold-locked).
